h1: Corner welding machines — TIG and plasma corner welders for bent boxes, cabinets and enclosures
intro: A corner welding machine welds the corners of bent sheet-metal parts — boxes, cabinets, trays, enclosures, hoods — with the torch carried by the machine at a set speed instead of by hand, so every corner is the same and the welder is free while it runs. NovoTech sells the CWS 200 and CWS 300 of Gecam, built in Parma, Italy: the part is clamped from inside against copper blocks that hold the corner square and draw off the heat, the TIG or plasma torch runs along a guide at 0 to 118 in/min, and the CNC touch screen stores the parameters of every part. Mild steel, stainless steel and aluminum; corners 7-7/8″ or 11-13/16″ high, parts from 3-15/16″ to 59″ square. The welded corner then goes to a corner grinder. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON.

groups.lead: Two corner heights, the same machine: clamp, start, and the torch welds the corner.

faq.q: What does a corner welding machine do?
faq.a: It welds the corner seam of a bent part with the torch on a guide, moved by the machine at a set speed: the operator places the part, clamps it with a button and presses start. The result is a straight, even weld on every corner, made in the flat position whatever the operator's skill, and the welder can prepare the next part while it runs.

faq.q: What do the copper blocks do?
faq.a: The part is pressed from inside against copper blocks — an external guide 7-7/8″ or 11-13/16″ high and an internal unit matched to the corner height. They hold the corner square during welding and draw the heat away, keeping the part cool and the weld zone clean; a cooling unit for the copper is available and recommended against discoloration.

faq.q: TIG or plasma — and is the power source included?
faq.a: The CWS works with a TIG or a plasma welding power source, which carries the torch on the machine's guide. Tell us the material, thickness and corner you weld and we will quote the CWS with a matching power source, or connect yours.
Bent parts from 3-15/16 × 3-15/16″ to 59 × 59″ with corners up to 7-7/8″ high (CWS 200) or 11-13/16″ (CWS 300), on a 32-5/16 × 32-5/16″ table. Mild steel, stainless steel and aluminum.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
